The 143 Is a Benchmark Vehicles Camper Van That Blurs the Line Between Rugged and Refined
19 photos
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles
Meet 143, a project based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 3500 XD with a 170" wheelbase. It's one of the latest builds by Benchmark Vehicles, a Portland, Oregon-based company specializing in custom adventure vehicles, mostly based on vans but also other types of vehicles. This project's name explanation is simple – this is the company's 143rd build.
Benchmark Vehicles creates super capable mobile homes – we've covered some of them here on autoevolution, like this family-friendly rig . Since the company applied the same design philosophy with the 143, you can tell that this is a roam-ready mobile home.
For starters, the van rides on Owl Vans Talon wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. The builders went even further in improving the vehicle's off-roading capabilities by installing an Agile Offroad ride improvement package with Fox shocks and Bilstein struts.
Off-roading can be quite tough on a vehicle – that's why Benchmark Vehicles added some extra protection. First, it applied an XPEL clear matte PPF (paint protection film) wrap to the body. Second, it covered the side rocker panels and part of the front bumper in truck bed liner.
Benchmark Vehicles made sure this van can go further by replacing the stock fuel tank with an S&B 40-gallon (151-liter) fuel tank.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles At the front, you'll come across grille-mounted TripleR lights and an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) bumper complete with a skid plate and a Warn Evo VR12S winch rated for 12,000 lb. (5,447 kg). What's more, there are two solar panels mounted on the hood for a total capacity of 245 W.
The opposite end was also put to great use. A spare tire carrier/ladder combo sits on the left side, while a large carrier with a cargo box takes up the right side. Moreover, underneath, there's a Van Compass Rear Rug step bumper.
Climb on top of the van, and you'll find a large Paragon Offroad rack. It holds a front-facing 50-inch Rigid light bar, a Starlink antenna, solar panels, and a 12-foot Girard power awning. Together with the hood solar panels, the total capacity stands at 416 W.
Other notable mods are Owl Vans side steps, power and water hookups (with plugs for both EU and US), and flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles Normally, builders do that to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the normal north to south. In this van, however, that's not the case – they create some space beside the bed to store things. This rig's flares are also paint matched to the van's body and come with Arctic Tern awning-style windows.
Enter, and you'll be surrounded by a large, almost apartment-like interior. Benchmark Vehicles shared that its interior department was tested to its limit on this Sprinter because of the complexity of the personalized design the customer wanted. This is the customer's third Sprinter, so they knew exactly what they wanted.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the rest of the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've parked.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for laminated cabinetry with a grain finish, grey woven flooring, and a cream-colored ceiling with matching walls. The look is complemented by white solid surface countertops and black accents, such as the cabinet and drawer handles.
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across a sizeable counter. It has a large top and a cabinet. Above, you'll find a swiveling fan and a decently sized cabinet.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units. The unit on the passenger side offers all the meal prep space you need thanks to its super long countertop. It also features a deep stainless steel sink with a pull-out faucet, a slide-out housing a coffee machine, and a portable stove.
The unit on the opposite side houses an overhead cabinet, a tall fridge with a freezer compartment, and a drawer at the bottom. A variety of storage compartments are available in the kitchen, including two overhead cabinets and seven drawers.
For storing clothes, you can use a floor-to-ceiling unit integrating two closets with hanging space.
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles Just like most deluxe camper vans, this Sprinter comes with a bathroom, hidden behind a tall conventional door. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a tiny corner shelf, and a Trelino composting toilet. Moreover, the back wall has a window and two L-Tracks for hanging clothes and towels.
This van has the perfect setup for relaxing after a long day out – you'll discover that the rear part of the living space is taken up by a huge king-size bed. The bedroom also offers two reading lights and charging points.
Finally, a roomy garage sits underneath the bedroom and is accessible from both inside and outside the van. In the middle, it offers a pull-out tray attached to heavy-duty slides that makes it easier to load and unload your items.
The garage's sides are partly taken up by two large boxes that accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 3,000 W inverter and a battery bank with a capacity of just under 1,000 Ah.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 35-gallon (132-liter) freshwater tank with heating pads mounted underneath the vehicle and not one but two under-mounted greywater tanks, also heated. A propane canister sits under the van, beside the freshwater tank.
There are two more important systems in this rig. The first is a diesel-powered Espar heater that provides heated air and water and also powers a radiant floor heating system. The second is a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit.
All in all, the 143 by Benchmark Vehicles combines serious off-road capability with a cozy, four-season-ready living space. Its interior design not only makes a lot of sense functionality-wise but it also makes you feel like you're in an actual home on wheels.
